title: Ian Macomber essay on post-AI data stack and company reality
summary: Ramp Head of Data essay arguing AI makes analysis cheap but consensus expensive: post-AI teams build a data-agent harness, governed semantic layer, and feedback loop so agents read llms.txt artifacts instead of inventing metrics.
question_it_answers: What architecture does Ian Macomber propose for a post-AI company data stack?

claims.text: Post-AI data teams must enable self-serve AI analysis and champion one singular company reality.
claims.evidence: Enable everyone to build with data and AI — accurately, powerfully, independently.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: Agent-readable dashboards should ship per-data-product llms.txt with owners, filters, and provenance instructions.
claims.evidence: Per-data-product `llms.txt` in markdown — code, filters, owners, entry points, rendered values.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: Semantic layer plus dbt tests act as the contract layer so agents do not invent metric definitions.
claims.evidence: Semantic layer + dbt tests as the contract layer.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge
